features.feature: Background tasks: commands, scheduled /loop, log monitors, prompt queue
features.how: Agent starts dev servers/builds as background tasks on its own (Ctrl+G pane, x to kill, Ctrl+B demotes a foreground command to background). /loop 5m <prompt> runs recurring prompt turns (min 60s, 7-day expiry, max 50 active). Monitors attach to a script so EACH output line becomes a conversation notification (watch CI/deploy logs). Prompts typed during a running turn are queued, not dropped (Ctrl+; queue panel).

features.feature: Hooks: lifecycle events, blocking PreToolUse, Claude/Cursor file compat
features.how: JSON hook files (~/.grok/hooks, .grok/hooks with trust gate) with command AND http endpoint types. Events: SessionStart/End, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse (only blocking event — returns {"decision":"deny"} JSON, exit 2 denies, everything else fail-open), PostToolUse(+Failure), PermissionDenied, Stop(+Failure), Notification, SubagentStart/Stop, PreCompact/PostCompact. Grok also READS Claude Code .claude/settings.json and Cursor .cursor/hooks.json hook files, mapping Claude tool names automatically.

features.feature: MCP with doctor diagnostics and cross-vendor config ingestion
features.how: `grok mcp add/list/remove/doctor --json`; stdio and HTTP transports with automatic OAuth (tokens in ~/.grok/mcp_credentials.json); ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} expansion in command/args/env/headers/urls; per-server startup_timeout_sec and tool_timeout_sec; project scope writes .grok/config.toml and walks cwd→git root, project overrides user by name. Also loads ~/.claude.json, .cursor/mcp.json, .mcp.json (per-vendor disable via [compat.claude] mcps=false). /mcps extensions tab toggles/authenticates servers live.

features.feature: Skills + plugins + marketplace, and zero-config Claude Code compatibility
features.how: Skills are SKILL.md folders with YAML frontmatter (when-to-use, paths gitignore-gating visibility, user-invocable→slash command, disable-model-invocation); plugins bundle skills+agents+hooks+MCP+LSP servers; TUI Marketplace tab browses/installs from configured sources (official catalog: github.com/xai-org/plugin-marketplace). Docs claim: 'Grok is fully compatible with Claude Code with zero configuration' — auto-reads Claude marketplaces, plugins, skills, MCPs, agents, hooks, CLAUDE.md/.claude/rules, plus AGENTS.md family and ~/.agents/skills+commands.

features.feature: Layered AGENTS.md rules with per-subtree scoping and verification
features.how: Loads global ~/.grok rules, then every dir from repo root to cwd (deeper wins), reading AGENTS.md/AGENT.md/CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md + .grok/rules/*.md (+ .claude/rules, .cursor/rules for compat); gitignored files skipped; nested AGENTS.md scopes a monorepo subtree; files loaded in full, no size cap. `--rules` appends, `--system-prompt-override` replaces. `grok inspect` lists every discovered rules file with path and approximate token count.

features.feature: Any-provider model config + separate routed web_search model
features.how: config.toml [models] default = "grok-build" for agent sessions and web_search = "grok-4.6" for the client-side search tool — search is routed to its own model. Per-model block: model id, base_url, env_key, api_backend = chat_completions|responses|messages, temperature/top_p/max_completion_tokens/context_window, extra_headers, supports_backend_search (enables Grok-hosted server-side search). GROK_MODELS_BASE_URL points at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint and lists models from {base}/models. Switch with -m/--model or /model, reasoning effort with /effort/--effort.

features.feature: Client-side web tools + server-side hosted search including X Search
features.how: CLI ships web_search (on by default, disable with --disable-web-search, model routed via GROK_WEB_SEARCH_MODEL) and web_fetch (OFF by default for security, GROK_WEB_FETCH_PROXY egress proxy support). For endpoints with supports_backend_search, the agent can use xAI's server-side built-in tools, whose catalog is Web Search, X Search (xSearch — real-time search over X posts), Code Interpreter, Image Generation, Collections Search. X integration is therefore via the API's built-in X Search tool rather than a dedicated CLI command.

features.feature: Five-scope config with enterprise policy pins and Claude Code flag aliases
features.how: Scopes: env (GROK_*), user ~/.grok/config.toml, project .grok/config.toml (deliberately limited to MCP/plugins/permissions only), managed_config.toml (MDM-served defaults), requirements.toml (policy pins that can override the CLI, e.g. forcing a sandbox). /settings modal, GROK_HOME relocation, `grok inspect` shows everything discovered. Accepts Claude Code flag names as aliases: --allowedTools, --disallowedTools, --append-system-prompt, --system-prompt, --dangerously-skip-permissions; legacy approval_mode/yolo keys still honored.

features.feature: OIDC, login restriction, managed sandbox/permission locks, ZDR
features.how: Enterprise OIDC or external auth provider, restricting allowed login methods (incl. team UUID allowlists), managed config for MDM deployment, headless dontAsk permission mode, sandbox/permission policy pins, documented network allowlist/TLS/proxy requirements, and Zero Data Retention tier.

features.feature: Cloud teammates (Grok Bot) and Claude Code delegation plugin
features.how: Grok Bot: persistent named AI teammates on a shared user-scoped cloud VM (browser, filesystem, terminal), running in parallel, messaging each other and handing off tasks, learning routines from live demonstration, reachable from desktop/mobile apps — the cloud counterpart to the local CLI. Separately, xai-org/grok-build-plugin-cc is an official Claude Code marketplace plugin that shells out to the grok CLI (status/results/stop via PID+log files) so Claude Code can delegate work to Grok Build.

tui_ux_highlights: Fullscreen, mouse-interactive TUI (not inline REPL): scrollback is a navigable list — Tab focuses it, vim j/k or arrows select entries, Shift+H/L jump per-turn, h/l collapse/expand, Enter opens a block in a fullscreen viewer, / searches scrollback, r toggles raw markdown (https://docs.x.ai/build/keyboard-shortcuts)

Interject mid-turn: Ctrl+Enter sends input while the agent is still running; prompts typed during a turn queue instead of dropping (Ctrl+; panel) (https://docs.x.ai/build/keyboard-shortcuts, https://docs.x.ai/build/features/background-tasks)
Plan review as a dedicated approval screen with per-line comments (a/s/c/q keys) shown even in auto/yolo modes (https://docs.x.ai/build/features/plan-mode)

Live status line above the shortcuts bar with three modes: builtin (model, context fill, cost) or `command` — Grok pipes current session data as JSON into your shell script on a timer (https://docs.x.ai/build/features/status-line)

Theme system: 5 built-in themes with live preview picker, truecolor-only themes hidden on lesser terminals, and theme="auto" that follows OS light/dark within seconds (https://docs.x.ai/build/features/theming)

Two panes for mental state: Ctrl+T todo pane (plan of record, survives resume) vs Ctrl+G tasks pane (running processes, loops, monitors) (https://docs.x.ai/build/features/sessions, https://docs.x.ai/build/features/background-tasks)

/terminal-setup diagnostic command plus `grok wrap ssh/docker/kubectl ...` — a local PTY that intercepts OSC 52 so clipboard copies over SSH reach your local machine (https://docs.x.ai/build/cli/terminal-support)

Per-terminal keyboard chord documentation (VS Code/Cursor/Zed, Apple Terminal, WezTerm kitty protocol, Zellij unlock mode) with concrete fixes instead of silent breakage (https://docs.x.ai/build/keyboard-shortcuts)

In-agent multimodal/workflow commands: /imagine and /imagine-video generate media, /deep-research runs background research, /create-workflow + /workflows give a live workflow-run dashboard, /btw asks a side question without interrupting the turn (https://docs.x.ai/build/modes-and-commands)

/feedback pipes bugs straight to the team from inside the session; /release-notes shows the changelog for the running version (https://x.ai/news/grok-build-cli, https://docs.x.ai/build/modes-and-commands)
would_steal_for_zcode: Zero-config cross-harness compatibility as an adoption wedge: auto-read Claude Code AND Cursor AND AGENTS.md ecosystem files (hooks, MCP configs, skills, agents, rules incl. .claude/rules and CLAUDE.local.md, gitignore-respected) with per-vendor disable switches — a GLM-native CLI that inherits users' existing Claude Code setups on first launch

`inspect` command: one command that dumps everything the agent discovered for the current directory (rules files with token counts, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP servers with origin, config sources) — makes config debugging deterministic

Clean two-layer safety model: permissions (does this call run: ask/auto-classifier/always-approve + allow/deny patterns) strictly separated from sandbox (what an approved call may touch: Landlock/Seatbelt profiles + custom deny globs), with a published limitations table instead of overselling
Session rewind = file snapshots + conversation truncation per prompt; sessions store tool calls AND file snapshots so state restore is exact; /fork for peer branching with optional worktree isolation

Background work as a first-class triad: agent-initiated background commands (Ctrl+B demotion), scheduled /loop prompt turns with expiry caps, and log-line MONITORS that inject one notification per matching line into the conversation — plus a prompt queue so typed input is never dropped mid-turn

Agent Dashboard as the multi-agent cockpit: state-grouped rows, peek panel, inline permission answering by number key, and dispatching NEW sessions directly into git worktrees from the dashboard input bar

Model routing granularity: a separate routed model for the web_search tool (cheap fast searcher vs main coder), per-model api_backend selection (chat_completions|responses|messages), context_window declared per model, and GROK_MODELS_BASE_URL pointing the whole CLI at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — exactly what a GLM-native zcode needs for glm-5 + a cheap flash model
Plan-file gate: while planning, ONLY the session plan file is writable and the plan review UI cannot be skipped even in yolo mode — a simple invariant that makes plan mode trustworthy

Hooks contract with explicit semantics: named events incl. SubagentStart/Stop and PreCompact, PreToolUse as the single blocking event, JSON stdin + env vars, documented fail-open behavior, and a /hooks-trust trust gate for project-provided hooks

LSP as a default-OFF single tool and tool_search for on-demand MCP tool discovery instead of loading whole toolsets — proof you can ship a top-tier agent without always-on indexing (no repo map anywhere in the official docs)

Honest provenance in the open repo: THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES declaring in-tree source ports of openai/codex and sst/opencode tool implementations — copying proven tool behavior openly with license notices is a legitimate design move
Diff UX defaults: one-line +N/-M collapsed edit blocks and folded read/search tool rows keep scrollback dense; raw-markdown and fullscreen block viewer on demand
